task: 28.75 — QA honesty: overlap ordering (L1), pixel width band (L3), page-state normalization (B7), false-alarm review (M6)
rubricComparability: A rubric-6 verdict may be WORSE (L1 can only add findings), BETTER (B7 can only remove findings, and only on pairs whose two sides are in different page states) or unchanged than the rubric-5 verdict of the same pair on the same clone. Rubric-5 and rubric-6 verdicts must NOT be compared, summed, or used as each other's floor. floorFrom already refuses a floor whose rubricVersion differs; this bump is what makes it refuse. EVERY self-check floor must be re-measured under rubric 6 before any rubric-6 verdict is read against one.

l1.defect: src/responsive-qa/overlap.ts:113-131 classifyOverlapPair tested the image load flag FIRST, before any geometry or ownership test, and fired when EITHER leaf failed. A real geometric collapse between two different visual owners was therefore demoted from the BLOCKER-capable overlap-excess-ratio to the MAJOR-only image-layer-state whenever one participant's asset did not decode. overlap-excess-ratio-undemoted went to rubric.record(), which takes no bands, so no amount of demoted area could move a verdict.
l1.fix: Geometry and ownership decide first: a pair is demotable only when both leaves are images with the same visual owner occupying the same box to within DUPLICATE_IMAGE_LAYER_TOLERANCE_PX on every edge (ONE PICTURE DRAWN TWICE). Inside that population the load flag chooses failed-image-layer over duplicate-image-stack. Everything else is true-overlap.
l1.principled: The demotion asserts 'these two boxes are one thing on screen'. That is self-evident for a under its own or a crossfade, and false for two different components in one place. Whether a resource decoded is a fact about the network; whether two owners occupy one rectangle is a fact about layout; the first is not evidence about the second. A broken keeps the box its CSS gives it.
l1.newChannelBands: BLOCKER 0.10 / MAJOR 0.02 / MINOR 0.001 — the overlap channel's OWN bands, unchanged and untuned; the populations are disjoint so it cannot double-count
l1.newChannelRationale: The source is rendered by the same browser at the same width under the same pinning policy, so both of the guard's explanations apply to it too. A genuine platform artefact cancels exactly; demoted area that does not cancel is area the clone piled up and the guard excused with an explanation the source refuses to corroborate.
l1.mutationProof: baseline fixture PASS/0 findings -> same fixture with clone duplicateImageStackAreaRatio 0.2 and source 0.0 -> BLOCKER, finding overlap-demoted-excess-ratio:BLOCKER, demotions.overlapFindingDemoted=true, demotions.demotedOverlapRegraded=true, demotions.demotedOverlapExcessRatio=0.2, and overlap-excess-ratio NOT also fired. Negative controls: the same demoted area on both sides cancels; a source stacking more than the clone can never fire it.
l1.realCorpusEvidence: Both demotion populations are EMPTY on every real pair measured to date: duplicateImageStackPairCount and failedImageLayerOverlapPairCount are 0/0 on source and clone across linear.app 2026-09-04T22-53-25-263Z (2 pairs), hobbang.net 2026-09-04T18-17-44-481Z (6 pairs), gs.severance.healthcare 2026-09-04T22-53-01-661Z (2 pairs) and seoultone.kr 2026-09-04T18-18-47-244Z (2 pairs), and again on the fresh 2026-09-04T23-40-51-897Z severance run (overlap-demoted-excess-ratio v=0 at both widths, coverage.overlapDemotionsRegraded=0). The reorder therefore changes no number on any canary run and the new channel reads exactly 0. FIXTURE-PROVED ONLY, and stated as such.
assertionsCorrected: an overlap involving an image whose asset did not paint is attributed to the layer state -> a collision between two DIFFERENT owners is a real overlap even when one asset did not paint (=== "true-overlap")

the sweep counts the broken leaf and keeps its overlap OUT of the true-overlap total -> ... AND keeps its collision with a different owner IN the true-overlap total (failedImageLayerOverlapPairCount 0, trueOverlapPairCount 1, trueOverlapArea > 0, broken leaf still counted)

l3.defect: src/responsive-qa/pixel-gate.ts:164-166 took a top-left-anchored min-crop and the comparison loop at :188-267 iterated only that region, with no field naming what was removed. The horizontal overflow band a frozen width produces is exactly the region deleted from the pixel evidence.
l3.optionChosen: A — compare on the common canvas, and report the excess band explicitly as its own quantity. Not B, because two differently-sized images have no common canvas without a resize (which would delete the finding a size difference IS), because marking the channels not-comparable would also lose the reading over the region that IS shared (86% of the page on severance @1100), and because the pixel channels can only ADD findings so keeping them eligible carries no false-PASS risk.
l3.fix: gatePixels keeps the identical comparison over the identical crop (every pre-existing number is bit-identical; the clone modal colour is derived in a SEPARATE pass so palette slot assignment and the modal tie-break are unchanged) and adds 19 fields: comparedWidth/Height, both actual capture sizes, widthMismatchPx/heightMismatchPx, per-side horizontal and vertical band pixel counts, per-side band INK counts (against that side's own modal colour), horizontalBandInkRatio, verticalBandInkRatio, comparedAreaRatio.
l3.conservationIdentity: 2 * comparedPixels + sum(four band pixel counts) == sourceArea + cloneArea — asserted in the suite on a one-axis and a both-axes/both-sides mismatch
l3.newChannelThreshold: PIXEL_UNCOMPARED_BAND_INK_MAJOR_RATIO, DEFINED IN CODE AS PIXEL_RESIDUAL_MINOR_RATIO (0.01) so the two cannot drift; derived, not chosen: if the strip that was never compared carries at least as much ink as the smallest pixel difference this rubric will report, that strip could by itself have carried a pixel finding.
l3.newChannelSeverity: MAJOR, because the channel does not report a difference — it reports that the instrument did not look. WP-C guard 4's rule (measurement failure is never green) applied to a partial measurement.
l3.verticalBandNotGraded: An unequal page HEIGHT is already a first-class finding on scroll-height-ratio-high / -low, and the strip it leaves uncompared is the bottom of a longer page, not a region any channel is investigating.
l3.compositeChange: composite.ts labelled 'source WxH / final WxH' in 12px grey. It now also prints a full-width red banner ('CAPTURE WIDTH MISMATCH — source 1280px vs final 1100px at a 1100px viewport. THESE TWO PANELS ARE NOT THE SAME WIDTH.') and hatches the uncompared strip in red on the wider panel with a '180px NOT PIXEL-COMPARED' label. renderComposite was split into a pure buildCompositeHtml so the suite asserts the banner, the hatch and both widths on the HTML.

b7.defect: normalizePageState had ZERO callers under src/responsive-qa/. captureSide (capture.ts:330-402) went goto -> stabilize -> pinMedia -> scroll -> probe -> screenshot and never normalized, while observe-page.ts:1335/:1100 does. The two instruments rendered the same URL into two different page states; on seoultone / @390 the source screenshot shows the entry popup, the clone correctly shows the hero, and the clone was charged missing-text-ratio for the popup's copy.
b7.quantified: @390 clone missing 393 chars (30.54%); popup accounts for 37 chars over 4 strings, real content loss for 356 chars (27.66%). @1440, popup present on both sides, missing is 356 chars — the same number.
b7.fix: captureSide now runs the two-call contract from the ONE shared implementation (src/observer/index.js): markInitialPaintCensus immediately after gotoQa and BEFORE stabilize, then normalizePageState after stabilize and BEFORE the scroll, the probe and the screenshot.
b7.bothSides: YES, and justified: the SOURCE side is the fix; the CLONE side is a CHECK (a reconstruction built from a normalized observation should have nothing left to dismiss, so page-state-clone-overlays-dismissed is expected to read 0 and a non-zero reading says the engine reproduced an entry popup); and captureSide exists so both sides are measured by literally the same code — normalizing one side only would replace this asymmetry with another and make the clone's state unobservable.
b7.recordedPerPair: SideProvenance.pageState (new PageStateRecord): ran, initialPaintCensusAvailable/Status/Elements/CapHit, qualified, dismissed, qualifiedNotDismissed, attemptCapHit, every attempt (domPath, shapeClass, method, outcome, signals, closeControlLabel), limitations. Plus three recorded channels: page-state-source-overlays-dismissed, page-state-clone-overlays-dismissed, page-state-comparable.
b7.notComparableRule: sourceOverlayStanding = source.pageState.ran AND (qualifiedNotDismissed > 0 OR attemptCapHit). When it holds, missing-text-ratio and visible-text-ratio are held INELIGIBLE with an ineligibleReason naming the count and the contract doc, the same reason is added to caveats, page-state-comparable records 0, and both channels keep their MEASURED value in channels[]. One-directional: a CLONE overlay standing gates nothing. An absent record grades exactly as before.
b7.evidenceRoot: QA_PAGE_STATE_EVIDENCE_ROOT = data/page-state-evidence/responsive-qa — outside docs/result/, mirroring the observer lane's own fix
b7.firesOnRealCorpus: MECHANISM PROVED IN A REAL BROWSER; the not-comparable BRANCH is fixture-only so far. The suite runs real Chromium against a served page reproducing the live seoultone popup shape: normalization OFF leaves the popup copy in the census and records ran=false; normalization ON reports dismissed 1 / qualifiedNotDismissed 0 / census available, removes the popup copy, keeps the page copy, and records the close-control attempt; the OBSERVER'S OWN API on the same page reaches the same state and agrees number for number on dismissed, qualified and initialPaintCensusStatus; and missingText from an un-normalized source charges the clone >0 chars while a normalized source charges it 0.0000. On the fresh gs.severance.healthcare run 2026-09-04T23-40-51-897Z both sides ran with census 'available' (1731 source / 3376 clone elements) and 0 qualified / 0 dismissed — the correct reading for a site with no entry popup — and page-state-comparable = 1 at both widths. The not-comparable branch has not been exercised by real corpus because no reachable canary site currently serves an undismissable entry overlay.

offscreenTextExcessChars.auditorFinding: BLOCKER on linear / @390 over 200 characters beginning past the right edge, on a product mock where the source itself bleeds
offscreenTextExcessChars.why_left_alone: The channel is ALREADY relative — classify.ts:455 computes clone.offscreenTextChars - source.offscreenTextChars — so the auditor's premise is subtracted by construction. On the cited pair the reading is value 200 with sourceValue 427: the source's own 427 off-screen characters are already removed. Three independent self-check (source-vs-source) runs — 2026-09-02T23-18-26-778Z, 2026-09-04T15-52-40-937Z, 2026-09-04T17-25-07-320Z — read excess 0 on / @390 against that same 427-character population, so the instrument is stable there and the 200 is a measured clone-minus-source delta. What remains is a judgement about the 80-character BLOCKER threshold, and moving it is the one move the rubric forbids.
offscreenTextExcessChars.principledAlternativeCarried: A difference of two TOTALS cannot distinguish 'the same strings, more of them' from 'different strings'. The correct measurement of the channel's own claim is a per-key excess over the source's off-screen census: sum over clone keys of max(0, cloneOffscreenChars[key] - sourceOffscreenChars[key]). NOT shipped, on evidence: on the same corpus it would FIRE where the current channel is silent (/ @700 reads -1206 today because the source parks 1,419 off-screen and the clone 213; a per-key reading would charge those 213 if they are strings the source keeps on screen), and the clone ships BOTH viewport subtrees, an unmeasured source of clone-only visible strings. A re-basing that can add BLOCKERs to four already-graded sites must be measured on those sites first, and the rubric-ordering rule puts that after this lane.

positionDeltaP90Px.auditorFinding: MAJOR at 63px against a 48px threshold on linear / @1440, a page the auditor could not fault
positionDeltaP90Px.why_left_alone: The principled comparison for a cross-side positional delta already exists in this harness and already runs: the self-check floor (item G4, --self-check), which runs this same rubric on the SOURCE against a second capture of ITSELF. On linear / @1440 three independent self-check runs read position-delta-p90-px = 0px, while the clone run 2026-09-04T17-25-07-319Z reads 63px. Source-against-source is ZERO, three times. The 'the source does it too' hypothesis is contradicted by the instrument's own control, and raising 48 -> 64 would delete a finding the floor says is real.
